title: The Gilded Sigil
premise: In the free city of Vellamare, where magic was outlawed a decade ago, Beatrix Zhou survives by carving bone charms that whisper with the voices of the dead she alone can hear. When the old gods suddenly begin answering prayers again, Beatrix's charms start screaming, and she learns the king of the realm died years ago—replaced by a hollow thing wearing his crown that feeds on memory itself. Hunted by the usurper's inquisitors, Beatrix gathers an unlikely found family: a disgraced priest, a god-touched child, and the ghost of her dead mentor. To save the free cities from the usurper's advancing armies, they must reach the capital and unbind the true king's soul from the crown-thing before it devours every memory of magic in the world. In the end, Beatrix sacrifices her own treasured memories of her mentor to complete the unbinding, freeing the king and restoring the gods—but discovering that loyalty outlives even what we forget.
about_author: Theo Thackeray is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent years restoring medieval bone reliquaries before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town where the fog rolls in like a second tide, writing stories about the things people refuse to forget.

chapters.title: The Quiet Trade
chapters.summary: Beatrix carves a mourning charm for a grieving widow, listening to the dead man's last words through the bone. Her POV establishes her hidden gift, her careful invisibility, and the loneliness of ten years of silence. Emotional beat: the ache of hearing what no one else can, and choosing to stay small.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: A charm Beatrix carved years ago begins to glow and speak on its own—the old gods are answering prayers for the first time since the Ban. Through her POV, terror and wonder collide as the dead grow louder. Emotional beat: the fragile safety of her hidden life cracking open.

chapters.title: The Priest Who Fell
chapters.summary: Disgraced priest Anselm Oduya arrives at Beatrix's shop, sent by a dying woman's prayer. His POV reveals he once helped enforce the Ban and now seeks absolution. He warns her the inquisitors are coming. Emotional beat: two people who broke the same law in opposite ways recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Inquisitors burn the shop of Beatrix's neighbor, a hedge-witch. Beatrix's POV follows her rescue of a god-touched orphan girl, Wren, whose prayers are being answered too literally. Emotional beat: guilt over years of complicit silence transforming into the first act of open defiance.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Fleeing Vellamare, the trio shelters in a charnel house where Beatrix hears a king's voice in ancient bone—a voice describing his own murder by 'the thing wearing my face.' Her POV. Emotional beat: horror giving way to terrible purpose; the dead have been waiting for someone to listen.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV on the road east: teaching Wren to pray safely while hiding from patrols. A quiet chapter of found family forming—shared meals, Wren's first laughter, Beatrix teaching Anselm to hear the dead. Emotional beat: tenderness taking root in dangerous ground.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Ghost
chapters.summary: Beatrix's dead mentor, Sefa, manifests fully for the first time, drawn back by the gods' return. Their reunion is joyful and barbed—Sefa disapproves of the quest's risks. Beatrix's POV. Emotional beat: grief complicated by second chances, and the fear of losing her again.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Convene
chapters.summary: In the city of Harrowgate, the free cities' council debates surrender versus resistance. Anselm's POV as he pleads their case, revealing the usurper's armies march within the month. Emotional beat: the frustration of watching institutions hesitate while children burn.

chapters.title: Wren's Prayer
chapters.summary: Wren, frightened by the council's cowardice, prays for help—and a minor god answers by flooding the harbor against a usurper fleet. Wren's POV, the novel's first child-eye view. Emotional beat: awe and terror entwined; divinity is not gentle, and Wren must decide if she is its vessel or its friend.

chapters.title: The Crown That Eats
chapters.summary: Beatrix communes with the murdered king's bone and sees visions of the crown-thing: a memory-devourer that consumed the king slowly, wearing him down until nothing was left but obedience. Her POV. Emotional beat: understanding that the enemy is not a tyrant but a hunger—and that memory is its food.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ford
chapters.summary: A council spy sells their route to the inquisitors. Ambush at a river ford; Sefa's ghost burns out holding the soldiers off. Beatrix's POV, raw with loss. Emotional beat: the cost of trust, and the discovery that ghosts, too, can choose sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Anselm infiltrates the capital disguised as a penitent priest and witnesses the crowned thing up close—it does not eat, sleep, or blink. His POV. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into clarity; the thing is weaker than it looks, sustained entirely by ritual and fear.

chapters.title: Gods in the Gutter
chapters.summary: Hiding in the capital's slums, Beatrix finds forgotten shrines waking in walls and wells. The small gods offer aid at prices paid in memory. Her POV. Emotional beat: temptation—she could trade away her worst memories and keep walking away from all this.

chapters.title: The Price of Forgetting
chapters.summary: Wren offers one of her own memories to a river god for safe passage beneath the palace. Beatrix stops her, furious, then confesses why: she once traded away a memory and has never known what it cost her. Beatrix's POV. Emotional beat: vulnerability as leadership; honesty about damage.

chapters.title: The King Beneath
chapters.summary: Beneath the palace, they find the true king's body preserved in bone—still faintly alive, kept as the crown-thing's anchor. Anselm's POV as he performs the forbidden rites of his old faith to stabilize the king's soul. Emotional beat: redemption earned in practice, not words.

chapters.title: Armies at the Gates
chapters.summary: The usurper's host arrives; the free cities' ragged defense begins. Wren's POV amid the chaos as she channels prayers from dying soldiers into a shield-wall of answered hopes. Emotional beat: courage without certainty; the found family scattered across a burning field.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Beatrix begins the unbinding, carving the king's soul free from the crown—but the rite demands a memory of equal love to replace what the crown consumed. Her POV. Emotional beat: the moment of choice, knowing exactly what will be asked.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: The crown-thing awakens and fights back, offering Beatrix illusions built from her own longing—including a false Sefa. Beatrix's POV, resisting by clinging to imperfection: real love includes grief. Emotional beat: the climax of identity; refusing a comfortable lie.

chapters.title: The Memory Given
chapters.summary: Beatrix surrenders her memories of Sefa to complete the unbinding. The true king's soul returns to his body; the crown-thing collapses into dust. She wakes not knowing who Sefa was, holding a bone charm she carved for someone she cannot name. Emotional beat: devastating triumph; victory that costs the self.

chapters.title: After the Dust
chapters.summary: The armies break as word spreads the king lives; the free cities hold. Anselm's POV on the aftermath—trials, reckonings, and his own choice to rebuild rather than atone forever. Emotional beat: weary hope; the world saved is still a world that must be mended.

chapters.title: The Charm Without a Name
chapters.summary: Beatrix, unable to remember Sefa, asks Wren to tell her about the ghost in her own memories. Wren recounts everything, and Beatrix chooses to carve a new charm so the story can be carried forward. Her POV. Emotional beat: grief transformed into inheritance; love that persists past forgetting.

chapters.title: The Listening City
chapters.summary: Months later, magic is legal again. Beatrix reopens her shop openly, training others to hear the dead, with Anselm and Wren beside her. The final image: a customer's charm whispers, and Beatrix smiles, listening. Emotional beat: belonging found at last—not invisible, but seen, and glad of it.
